case_name: Hitendra S/O. Vinayakrao Upadhyay vs The State Of Maharashtra And Anr

parties.respondent_defendant: The State Of Maharashtra And Anr

facts_of_case: Check bouncing case filed in 2017; evidence given in January 2018; accused moved for impounding of document but application rejected by J.M.F.C.; revision fled in Sessions Court but no stay granted.

legal_principles.principle: No prejudice will be caused to respondent No. 2, accused in that proceeding if direction of early disposal of the matter is given.
legal_principles.held: Notice is given only to the State and this Court held that there is no need to give notice to respondent No. 2 as no prejudice will be caused to respondent No. 2, accused in that proceeding if direction of early disposal of the matter is given.

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the accused to show that there is no prejudice if direction of early disposal of the matter is given.
legal_principles.held: In view of the requirements which are given in section 138 of Negotiable Instruments Act and aforesaid circumstances, this Court holds that there is no need to give notice to respondent No. 2 as no prejudice will be caused to respondent No. 2, accused in that proceeding if direction of early disposal of the matter is given.

outcome.final_order: Direction is hereby given to expeditiously dispose of the proceeding and in any case, within six months from the date of receipt of this order.

use_for_drafting: drafting a petition for early disposal of a proceeding
seeking direction to a court for expeditious disposal
challenging an order in Sessions Court
